title: CN Tower
blurb: Toronto’s 553.3 m concrete communications tower, the world’s tallest freestanding structure from 1976 to 2007: hexagonal shaft, seven-storey main pod with the Glass Floor, and the SkyPod at 447 m.

sourceUrls.label: LiwinCo: CN Tower Toronto City Guide

systems.name: Foundation and entrance
systems.description: The deep foundation slab and the entrance pavilion at the tower base.

systems.name: Concrete shaft
systems.description: The hexagonal concrete shaft rising 335 m, with its base flare, ribs and upper section.

systems.name: Main pod
systems.description: The seven-storey main pod with the 360 Restaurant and the EdgeWalk ledge on its roof.

systems.name: Glass floor
systems.description: The Glass Floor at 342 m, opened in 1994.

systems.name: SkyPod
systems.description: The smaller SkyPod at 447 m, one of the world's highest observation decks.

systems.name: Antenna
systems.description: The 96 m antenna spire with transmitter collars and beacon, reaching 553.3 m.

systems.name: Elevators
systems.description: High-speed elevator cars running up the shaft exterior at 6 m/s.

systems.name: Services
systems.description: The stairwell with 1,776 steps to the main level.
